# FDG5005

> DO NOT use `ref`, `out`, or `in` modifiers to overload members.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 5.1.1 Member Overloading.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (full coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG5005
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Do not overload '{0}' on the '{1}' modifier of the parameter '{2}'

FDG5005 reports a parameter with a `ref`, `out`, `in` or `ref readonly` modifier when another overload in the same type has the same parameter types without that modifier at that position. Overrides and interface implementations are not reported. Renaming or removing an overload changes the public API, so there is no code fix.

## From the book

For example, you should not do the following:

```csharp
public class SomeType {
  public void SomeMethod(string name){ ... }
  public void SomeMethod(out string name){ ... }
}
```

Some languages cannot resolve calls to overloads like this. In addition, such overloads usually have completely different semantics and probably should not be overloads at all, but rather two separate methods.
